name: debuganything

tools.name: readiness
tools.description: Report OS, arch, which providers (strace, py-spy, perf, lsof, tcpdump, gdb/lldb, docker...) are usable, what is missing and how to install it, and permission status (ptrace_scope, sudo, SIP). Always call this first.

tools.name: attach
tools.description: Resolve a target (pid, container, k8s pod, or a command to spawn under capture) and open a session. Returns session_id used by every other tool. Read-only: nothing is modified.

target.description: pid, container name/id, k8s pod (ns/name), or a command line (with kind=command)

kind.description: Defaults to auto-detect: numeric → pid, else container, else command

tools.name: detach
tools.description: Stop any running captures for the session, finalize the report, keep artifacts under ~/.debuganything/sessions/<id>/.

tools.name: list_processes
tools.description: ps-style list (pid, comm, cpu, mem, user, container) for picking a target. Optional substring filter.

filter.description: Substring match on command / args / user

tools.name: trace_syscalls
tools.description: Linux strace of the target for N seconds: top syscalls by total time and count, slowest individual calls, error counts (ENOENT/EAGAIN/ECONNREFUSED...), blocked waits. Raw log saved as artifact.

tools.name: profile_cpu
tools.description: CPU profile for N seconds: py-spy (Python), perf (native/Node on Linux), sample (macOS). Returns top frames (self/total), hottest stacks, flamegraph.svg artifact.

tools.name: dump_stacks
tools.description: Instant snapshot of every thread's stack (py-spy dump / gdb / lldb / Node inspector). The key tool for hangs and deadlocks; flags threads waiting on the same lock.

tools.name: inspect_sockets
tools.description: lsof/ss view of the target: listening ports, established connections grouped by remote, states (CLOSE_WAIT pileups, TIME_WAIT counts), fd count vs ulimit.

tools.name: inspect_files
tools.description: Open file descriptors by type, growth over a short window, largest open files, deleted-but-open files (disk full but nothing there).

window_s.description: Observe fd growth over this many seconds (0 = single snapshot)

tools.name: capture_traffic
tools.description: tcpdump scoped to the target's ports for N seconds (max 30). Per-remote bytes/packets, retransmits, RSTs, DNS queries, TLS SNI. .pcap artifact. REQUIRES consent: true — ask the user first.

filter.description: Extra BPF filter ANDed with the target's ports

consent.description: Required. Packet capture may contain secrets; ask the user first.

tools.name: snapshot_memory
tools.description: RSS/VSZ sampled over a window; Node: heap snapshot with top retainers by retained size; Python: py-spy dump with locals. Take two and diff_runs them to find what grows.

heap.description: Take a heap snapshot where supported (Node). Set false for metrics only.

window_s.description: Sample RSS over this many seconds

tools.name: diff_runs
tools.description: Diff two prior runs of the same tool in this session (e.g. snapshot_memory#1 vs snapshot_memory#2, profile_cpu#1 vs #2): what grew, appeared, disappeared.

a.description: run id of the earlier result; '<session_id>:<run>' reads a baseline run from another session (e.g. a recorded healthy run)

b.description: run id of the later result; '<session_id>:<run>' works here too

tools.name: container_info
tools.description: docker inspect/stats/top/logs tail for the target container, host pid mapping, cgroup limits: throttled? OOM-killed before? restarts?

tools.name: report
tools.description: Markdown report of the whole session: findings, evidence excerpts, artifact paths. Optionally written to a file.

out.description: Optional path to also write the markdown to

html.description: Also render a self-contained report.html (shareable: ranked findings, expandable evidence, embedded flamegraphs)

tools.name: import_artifact
tools.description: Analyze raw tool output you captured yourself (e.g. `sudo strace …`, `sudo fs_usage …`, `perf script`, `py-spy dump`, `lsof -F`, `tcpdump -nn -tt -r`) and turn it into the same evidence and findings Debug Anything would produce. Use when Debug Anything could not run the tool (no root, macOS).

path.description: Path to the raw output file you captured yourself (e.g. with sudo)

duration_s.description: How long the capture ran, when the file has no timestamps (profiles)

instructions: DebugAnything (Debug Anything) observes running processes, containers and pods with battle-tested local tools and returns structured evidence. Call readiness first, attach before anything else, detach at the end. Every finding cites evidence ids — never claim a root cause without one. capture_traffic requires consent: true; ask the user first. Read-only: Debug Anything never kills, signals or modifies the target. USE Debug Anything PROACTIVELY: when a command you ran hangs, a test times out, output shows EADDRINUSE / ECONNREFUSED / EMFILE / exit 137 / OOM / segfault, a server you started does not respond, or the user mentions slow, hang, leak, crash or a busy port — attach and measure (dump_stacks, inspect_sockets, profile_cpu, snapshot_memory, container_info) before proposing a theory, without waiting to be asked. After you change performance-sensitive code, re-measure and diff_runs to prove it.
